Extension API — What Seems Impossible But Isn't\n\nThe VS Code Extension API is remarkably deep:\n\n- **Virtual File System (`vscode.FileSystemProvider`)**: An extension can register a URI scheme (e.g., `myagent://`) and implement an entire file system. VS Code treats it identically to local disk — open, save, diff, Git all work. An agent empire could expose its entire knowledge graph as a browseable virtual filesystem.\n- **Custom Editors (`CustomEditorProvider`)**: Full control over any file type's editor — not just syntax highlighting but completely custom WebView rendering. Build a visual soul-ledger editor, a pipeline DAG visualizer, etc.\n- **Notebook API (`NotebookSerializer` + `NotebookController`)**: Extensions can define entirely new notebook formats. A `NotebookController` executes cells and produces structured outputs (text, HTML, SVG, JSON, images). An agent pipeline could be authored as a notebook where each cell is an agent step.\n- **Webview Panels**: Extensions get a full sandboxed browser context — communicate with extension host via `postMessage`. Build any React/Vue UI inside VS Code with full access to extension APIs.\n- **Tree View API**: Custom sidebar panels with arbitrary tree structures, icons, and inline actions. Ideal for visualizing agent state, soul ledger entries, pipeline status.\n- **Language Model API (stable)**: Extensions can call `vscode.lm.selectChatModels()` to use whatever AI model the user has configured — Copilot, Claude, any registered provider — without managing API keys themselves.\n\n### 3. Task System — More Powerful Than Developers Realize\n\nThe Task Provider API is fully programmatic. An extension implementing `vscode.TaskProvider` can:\n- Detect workspace state and dynamically generate tasks\n- Return `CustomExecution` tasks that run in a pseudoterminal controlled by the extension (not a real shell), enabling full stdout/stderr intercept\n- Tasks can auto-trigger on `folderOpen` (the `runOptions.runOn` flag)\n- `vscode.tasks.executeTask()` runs any task programmatically from extension code\n\n**Practical use**: An agent orchestrator extension could spawn, monitor, and chain tasks without ever touching the terminal directly.\n\n### 4. LSP — Build a Custom Code Intelligence Server for AI\n\nLSP is now arguably more valuable for AI agents than for humans. Key developments:\n\n- **LSP-AI** (open source, GitHub: `SilasMarvin/lsp-ai`) is a language server that acts as an AI backend — any LSP-capable editor gets AI completions without IDE-specific plugins.\n- Claude Code shipped native LSP support (v2.0.74, December 2025), giving it `goToDefinition`, `findReferences`, `hover`, `documentSymbol`, and `getDiagnostics` as first-class tools instead of grep.\n- **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**: An emerging JSON-RPC standard (called \"LSP for AI agents\") that breaks the 1:1 editor-to-agent coupling. ACP is the next layer up from LSP.\n- **VSCode-LSP MCP server**: There's a marketplace MCP server that exposes LSP operations to any MCP-capable agent, meaning an external agent (not running inside VS Code) can query live code intelligence from a running VS Code instance.\n\n**Hidden gem**: A custom LSP server can provide semantic context about your *specific* codebase — soul keywords, canonical patterns, forbidden patterns — injected into any AI's context automatically on every edit.\n\n### 5. Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) — Fully Automatable\n\nDAP is language-agnostic and completely automatable:\n- `DebugAdapterInlineImplementation` — implement DAP as a TypeScript object inside an extension, with full control over all debug events\n- `DebugAdapterServer` — connect to an external process via TCP, enabling remote debug control\n- An extension can call `vscode.debug.startDebugging()`, set breakpoints programmatically via `vscode.debug.addBreakpoints()`, and listen to all debug events (stopped, continued, output, terminated)\n- An AI agent could run code, catch exceptions, read the stack trace and variables, patch the code, and re-run — entirely without human input\n\n**This is the missing piece**: most AI coding agents edit code but can't close the feedback loop with actual runtime state. DAP gives that loop.\n\n### 6. Multi-Root Workspaces — Agent Isolation Architecture\n\nVS Code 1.107 (November 2025) made this concrete: **background agents use Git worktrees for isolation**. Each background agent session gets its own worktree — multiple agents can work on different branches simultaneously without conflicting edits.\n\n**Creative uses:**\n- Open `APPS/NET-PET-AI`, `D:\\PROJECTS\\phoenix-coder`, and `D:\\OB-1-CANONICAL` as a single multi-root workspace. Copilot instructions from all three repos merge and are concatenated into every prompt.\n- Assign different agents to different workspace roots — one agent owns the API, another owns the frontend, a third monitors the DB.\n- Cross-repo search and context: Copilot can search and correlate code across all roots simultaneously.\n\n### 7. VS Code Remote (SSH, Containers, WSL) — Agent Sandboxing\n\nDevContainers are now the consensus answer to safe AI agent execution:\n- `devcontainer.json` defines the exact environment — the agent's blast radius is the container, not the host\n- If an agent runs `rm -rf /`, rebuild the container — SSH keys, host credentials untouched\n- Copilot auto-pulls custom instructions from container images\n- VS Code Remote SSH lets agent sessions run on cloud VMs and continue after disconnect\n\nVS Code's remote architecture deliberately separates UI from backend — the Extension Host runs on the remote machine, the rendering runs locally.\n\n### 8. Extension Host — Headless Status\n\nTrue headless extension execution (running extensions without any UI) remains an **open feature request** as of 2025. The VS Code Server does run headlessly, but it serves a web client — it's not a pure programmatic execution environment. The community workaround is running VS Code Server in a container and connecting via the web UI. Roo Code and similar agent extensions specifically called out headless CLI execution as a missing capability (GitHub issue #3835).\n\n**What does work headlessly**: the VS Code Server binary can be invoked for file serving, terminal, and extension tasks via the remote connection. The `--extensionDevelopmentPath` flag can be used for automated extension testing in CI without a display.\n\n### 9. code-server / openvscode-server\n\n- **`code-server`** (Coder): Full VS Code in a browser tab, served from any machine. Enables running the entire dev environment on a cloud VM or Raspberry Pi while working from a browser.\n- **`openvscode-server`** (Gitpod): The upstream VS Code server, no Coder branding. Deployable in Docker.\n- **What this enables**: Each agent gets its own VS Code instance running in a container, accessible via browser. You can manage an empire of 10 parallel VS Code instances, each running a different branch/task, monitored from a single browser.\n\n### 10. GitHub Copilot Workspace vs Kilo/Claude Code\n\n| Dimension | Copilot Workspace | Claude Code / Kilo |\n|---|---|---|\n| Entry point | GitHub issue / PR | CLI / extension |\n| Context window | 128k tokens | Up to 1M tokens |\n| Agent locus | IDE-embedded | Terminal-first |\n| Multi-file reasoning | Yes, issue-to-PR | Yes, repo-wide |\n| Sub-agent isolation | No equivalent | Spawns sub-agents with isolated context |\n| SWE-bench score | 33.2% (Copilot) | 72.5% (Claude Code); 87.6% (Opus 4.7) |\n| Best use | Inline completion flow | Autonomous multi-step engineering |\n\nThey operate at different layers — use both. Copilot for moment-to-moment flow; Claude Code/Kilo for deliberate engineering.\n\n### 11. Extensions Worth Having in an AI Agent Empire\n\n- **Cline** (5M installs, 61k GitHub stars): Open-source VS Code agent, Plan/Act workflow, supports 30+ model providers. Best open-source alternative to Copilot agent mode.\n- **Aider**: Commits code as git commits — every change is a safe undo point. Runs from terminal but has VS Code integration.\n- **Git Graph**: Visual commit graph. Critical for monitoring parallel agent branches.\n- **GitLens**: Inline blame, file history, remote tracking — essential for understanding what agents changed.\n- **LSP-AI**: Provides AI completions via LSP to any editor without IDE-specific glue.\n- **REST Client / Thunder Client**: API testing inline — agents can verify their own deployed endpoints.\n- **Dev Containers extension**: Required for sandbox isolation.\n- **Remote SSH**: Connect to cloud VM agent workloads.\n\n### 12. Jupyter Notebook Integration\n\nVS Code has deep Jupyter support. For AI pipelines this matters because:\n- `/newNotebook` slash command in Copilot chat generates an entire notebook from a prompt\n- Agent mode can edit across multiple cells simultaneously\n- `NotebookController` API lets a custom extension execute cells against any runtime (Python kernel, custom agent runner, etc.)\n- Jupyter AI (JupyterLab extension) integrates Claude, Gemini, Copilot via ACP — agents can read and write files, run terminal commands, and interact with notebooks via a built-in Jupyter MCP server\n- **Pipeline use case**: Each pipeline stage (RRL → SOUL → DNA → CryptoHeavyLedger) could be a notebook cell with structured outputs, checkpointed and resumable.\n\n---\n\n## AREA 2: GOOGLE'S FULL AI DEVELOPER PLATFORM\n\n### 1. Gemini API Free Tier — Actual Current Limits (May 2026)\n\n**Important**: Google tightened the free tier significantly. As of April 1, 2026, Pro models are no longer free. Current state:\n\n| Model | RPM (free) | RPD (free) | Context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Gemini 2.5 Pro | 5 RPM | 100 RPD | 1M tokens |\n| Gemini 2.5 Flash | 10 RPM | 250 RPD | 1M tokens |\n| Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite | 15 RPM | 1,000 RPD | 1M tokens |\n\nAll models: 250,000 tokens/minute shared limit. Gemini 2.0 Flash is deprecated and shuts down June 1, 2026. Gemini 3.x (including 3.1 Pro, launched Feb 19, 2026) is paid-only. **Flash-Lite at 1,000 RPD free is the sleeper pick** for high-frequency lightweight tasks.\n\n### 2. Gemini 2.5 Pro — What 1M Token Context Actually Enables\n\n- 100% recall up to 530,000 tokens; 99.7% recall at 1M\n- Processes ~1,500 pages of text or ~30,000 lines of code in a single call\n- Entire repositories can be passed as context — no chunking, no RAG required for medium codebases\n- **What no other model enables at this scale**: analyze a full codebase for architectural patterns, summarize an entire conversation history without lossy compression, ingest complete legal documents or research papers, pass multi-hour audio/video transcripts\n- MCP native support in the Gemini API/SDK\n- Built-in \"thinking\" mode — Gemini 2.5 Pro reasons through problems before answering (like o1/o3)\n- **For OB-1**: Could ingest the entire CANON directory plus all pipeline output in a single call for deep synthesis\n\n### 3. Gemini Nano — Chrome Prompt API (Hidden Gem)\n\n**This is a genuine sleeper.** Gemini Nano runs entirely on-device via WebAssembly/WebGPU in Chrome. No API key, no network call, no cost. Available APIs:\n\n- `window.ai.createTextSession()` — Prompt API\n- Summarizer API\n- Translator API (native languages, no Google Translate API key)\n- Writer / Rewriter API\n- Proofreader API\n- **Multimodal support**: image and audio input\n\n**Chrome Extensions get full access** to all of these. Available on Windows 10/11, macOS 13+, Linux, ChromeOS Plus. Origin Trials expected to become permanent in Chrome 145-150.\n\n**Hidden gem use case**: A Chrome extension that intercepts YouTube, Google Docs, Gmail, any web page and runs local Gemini Nano inference on the content — zero API cost, works offline, no rate limits. For the student Chrome extension OB-1 already contemplates, this is significant — grammar correction, translation, content summarization all free and local.\n\n### 4. Google AI Studio\n\nFree, no subscription, no seat fee. Current capabilities:\n- Prompt engineering for all Gemini models\n- Grounding with Google Search: 1,500 RPD free, then $35/1K\n- Grounding with Google Maps: 500 RPD free\n- System instructions, few-shot examples, structured output configuration\n- Fine-tuning available via Vertex AI (not AI Studio directly)\n- **Workspace API integration** (new at I/O 2026): Agents built in AI Studio can natively call Google Sheets, Docs, Drive APIs\n- **Custom agent templates**: Define agent behavior in markdown (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md) — directly analogous to OB-1's own CLAUDE.md architecture\n- Project export: one-click migration from AI Studio prototype to local Antigravity development\n\n### 5. Vertex AI Free Tier — What's Actually Free\n\nVery limited for production; useful for prototyping:\n- Vertex AI Studio: free with rate limits (up to 1,000 req/day for some models)\n- Agent Engine runtime: 50 vCPU-hours + 100 GB-hours/month free\n- Workbench notebooks: limited free compute hours\n- Express Mode: 10 agent engines, 90-day sandbox, no billing required\n- $300 free credits for new Google Cloud accounts (90-day expiry)\n\n**Verdict**: Vertex AI free tier is prototype-only. Once you add search retrieval ($4-6/1K), session state ($0.25/1K events), and Agent Engine compute, production costs stack fast. Use the Gemini API direct for cost-controlled agent workloads.\n\n### 6. Project IDX\n\nGoogle's cloud IDE — VS Code fork running in a browser, hosted on Google Cloud. Currently **free in preview**. Key facts:\n- Familiar VS Code UI, same extension marketplace\n- Gemini AI built in natively (not via extension)\n- Full terminal, devcontainers support\n- Firebase and Google Cloud services pre-wired\n- **Limitation**: Extension ecosystem smaller than VS Code desktop; collaboration less mature than GitHub Codespaces\n- **Best use case**: Spin up a throwaway Google-integrated dev environment without local setup. Good for student onboarding where you don't want to manage local installs.\n\n### 7. Google Colab — Free GPU\n\nReality check: Colab's free tier gives intermittent T4 GPU (15GB VRAM), sessions up to 12 hours, no persistence guarantees. **Not suitable for persistent agent workloads.** Use cases:\n- Fine-tuning small models (Gemma 2B/7B) in short bursts\n- One-off data processing pipelines\n- Experimenting with inference before committing to paid GPU\n\nColab Pro ($11.99/mo) or Pro+ ($49.99/mo) if you need reliable GPUs.\n\n### 8. Firebase Free Tier — Spark Plan\n\n| Service | Free Limit |\n|---|---|\n| Firestore reads | 50,000/day |\n| Firestore writes | 20,000/day |\n| Firestore storage | 1 GB |\n| Cloud Functions | 2M invocations/month |\n| Hosting storage | 1 GB |\n| Hosting transfer | 10 GB/month |\n| Analytics, FCM, Crashlytics | Unlimited, always free |\n\n**For an agent empire**: Firestore at 50k reads/day is real capacity for a lightweight agent state store. Cloud Functions at 2M/month can handle webhooks, triggers, and lightweight API endpoints entirely free. Firebase Hosting + Cloud Functions is a workable free-tier backend for student-facing tools.\n\n### 9. Google Cloud Run — 2M Requests Free\n\nConfirmed: 2 million requests/month free + 360,000 vCPU-seconds + 180,000 GiB-seconds. Beyond that: $0.40/million additional requests. **This is the right compute tier for agent API endpoints** — deploy a containerized agent as a Cloud Run service, it scales to zero when idle (no cost), handles burst traffic, and the free tier is substantial for low-to-medium volume workloads.\n\nCombined with Firebase for state and the Gemini API for inference, Cloud Run is the zero-cost backbone for a production agent API.\n\n### 10. Developer access paths:\n- **Apps Script + Gemini API**: Automate Docs, Sheets, Gmail, Calendar, Drive with Gemini inference\n- **Gemini Enterprise Agents**: Workspace add-ons for Chat/Gmail that extend to Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides\n- **AI Studio Workspace Integration** (new at I/O 2026): Agents in AI Studio can directly read/write Google Sheets, organize Drive files, interact with Docs\n\n### 11. It is:\n\n- A **VS Code fork** with an agent-first interface\n- **Free for individuals** in public preview, available now at `antigravity.google/download`\n- **Two modes**: Editor View (traditional AI-assisted IDE) + Manager Surface (spawn/orchestrate/observe multiple agents working asynchronously across workspaces)\n- Agents generate **Artifacts** — tangible deliverables (task lists, plans, screenshots, browser recordings) you can comment on like a Google Doc\n- **Chrome extension** for browser agents: agents can launch Chrome, scroll, click, type, inspect console logs autonomously\n- **Knowledge Base**: agents save useful context and code snippets, improving future task performance\n- Model support: Gemini 3 Pro (generous free limits), Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5/4.6, GPT-OSS-120B\n- **AGENTS.md and SKILL.md** architecture — directly mirrors OB-1's own CLAUDE.md system\n- **Antigravity 2.0** (announced I/O 2026 May 2026): dynamic sub-agents for parallel execution, scheduled background tasks, Android native support, Firebase integration, predictive scaling, native memory persistence\n- **Antigravity CLI**: lightweight terminal interface for instant agent creation without GUI\n\n**Why this matters for OB-1**: Antigravity is Google's direct answer to Claude Code / Kilo. Grounding API — Real-Time Web Search\n\nGemini's Grounding with Google Search is a native API capability:\n- `\"tools\": [{\"googleSearch\": {}}]` in any API call gives the model real-time web access\n- Model auto-generates search queries, synthesizes results, returns `groundingMetadata` (queries, web results, citations)\n- For Gemini 3 models: billed per search query the model executes\n- For Gemini 2.5 and older: billed per prompt (not per search)\n- 1,500 grounded prompts/day free\n- **Also available**: Grounding with Google Maps (500 RPD free) — enables location-aware agents\n\nThis is meaningfully different from RAG — it's live web search baked into the inference call, not pre-indexed retrieval.\n\n### 13. Here is the full intelligence report:\n\n---\n\n# OpenClaw / KiloClaw — Exhaustive Research Report for PCC\n\n---\n\n## 1. OpenClaw Architecture — Core Runtime\n\n**What it is:** OpenClaw is a personal AI agent runtime — not a coding assistant in the Cursor/Claude Code sense. It is a persistent local Gateway daemon (Node.js 22+) that owns messaging channels, routes messages through LLM agents, executes tools, and maintains memory. It was originally \"Clawdbot\" (November 2025), renamed \"Moltbot\" (January 27, 2026) after Anthropic trademark complaints, then \"OpenClaw\" three days later. Written in TypeScript + Swift. MIT licensed. Peaked at 247,000 GitHub stars / 47,700 forks by March 2026. Founder Peter Steinberger joined OpenAI on February 14, 2026; governance transferred to a non-profit foundation.\n\n**Core runtime loop:**\n\n```\nInbound message → Channel Adapter → Access Control → Session Resolution\n→ Context Assembly (AGENTS.md + SOUL.md + TOOLS.md + Memory Search)\n→ LLM Invocation (streaming, token-by-token)\n→ Tool Execution (sandboxed or native)\n→ Response Delivery → Session State Persistence\n```\n\n**Five core subsystems:**\n1. **Gateway Control Plane** — Single long-lived WebSocket server, `127.0.0.1:18789` by default. ALL clients connect here: CLI, web UI, macOS app, iOS/Android nodes, headless nodes. No REST API (WebSocket-only; HTTP REST is an open feature request). No microservices.\n2. **Channel Adapters** — WhatsApp (via Baileys), Telegram (grammY), Discord (discord.js), Signal, iMessage, Slack, Matrix, LINE, WeChat, QQ, Tlon, Zalo, Nostr, Twitch, Synapse, and 10+ more. Each normalizes platform-specific formats into the unified session model.\n3. **Agent Runtime** — Uses `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core`. Four-phase: session resolution → context assembly → model invocation → state persistence.\n4. **Tool System** — Browser (Playwright/CDP), bash exec (sandboxed or native), canvas, cron, session tools, platform-specific node actions (camera, location, screen).\n5. **Memory System** — SQLite per-agent with hybrid BM25 + vector search. `MEMORY.md` (curated facts), daily `.md` activity logs, session transcripts (experimental).\n\n**Key differences from Claude Code / Cursor:**\n- Cursor and Claude Code are IDE-embedded coding assistants. OpenClaw is a **messaging-platform-driven autonomous agent** that operates 24/7 as a daemon, can be triggered by WhatsApp messages, and orchestrates multi-agent pipelines with cron scheduling. It is closer to an \"AI operating system\" than a coding tool.\n- Coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) are treated as external sub-tools that OpenClaw can spawn via ACP.\n\n**Stack specifics:** Protocol version 4. Session storage at `~/.openclaw/sessions/` as append-only JSONL event logs with branching support. Config at `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (JSON5 format). Credentials at `~/.openclaw/credentials/` with 0600 permissions.\n\n---\n\n## 2. ACP — Agent Client Protocol\n\n**What it is:** ACP (Agent Client Protocol) is a stdio-based protocol for IDE/tool → agent communication. It speaks **NDJSON over stdio**, with the underlying transport to the OpenClaw Gateway being WebSocket.\n\n**Architecture:** OpenClaw does NOT implement a native ACP runtime. `openclaw acp` is a **Gateway-backed bridge** — it translates IDE ACP messages into Gateway WebSocket protocol. IDEs treat `openclaw acp` as their agent server process.\n\n**Wire format:**\n- Transport: stdio (for IDEs) ↔ WebSocket (to Gateway)\n- Frame format: NDJSON — one JSON object per line\n- Message metadata example:\n```json\n{\n  \"_meta\": {\n    \"sessionKey\": \"agent:main:main\",\n    \"sessionLabel\": \"support inbox\",\n    \"resetSession\": true\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Implemented protocol methods:**\n- `initialize`, `newSession`, `prompt`, `cancel`\n- `listSessions`, slash commands\n- `resumeSession`, `closeSession`\n- Session lineage metadata\n\n**Partially implemented:**\n- `loadSession` (full history only for bridge-created sessions)\n- Tool streaming\n- Exec approvals\n\n**NOT implemented (critical gaps):**\n- Per-session MCP servers — IDE-configured MCP tools are explicitly ignored (\"ignoring N MCP servers\")\n- Client filesystem methods (no unsaved buffer access)\n- Client terminal methods (no real-time output in IDE)\n- Session plans / thought streaming\n- Permission requests surfacing in IDE (OpenClaw's internal permission logic exists but was not wired into the ACP bridge)\n\n**Session key format:** `acp:&lt;uuid&gt;` by default (isolated per editor turn). Override with `--session agent:main:main` or `--session-label \"name\"`.\n\n**Critical behavioral bug:** Multiple ACP clients sharing one Gateway session key causes cross-wired cancellation — cancelling one session aborts all sessions on that key.\n\n**Supported harnesses (13 listed):** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, iFlow, Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, OpenCode, Qoder, Qwen, Trae.\n\n**IDE integration (Zed):**\n```json\n{\n  \"agent_servers\": {\n    \"OpenClaw ACP\": {\n      \"type\": \"custom\",\n      \"command\": \"openclaw\",\n      \"args\": [\"acp\"]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**`openclaw acp client`** — Built-in debug client to test the bridge without an IDE.\n\n**acpx** (separate project, `github.com/openclaw/acpx`) — A dedicated headless CLI abstraction layer that works across 17 agents (Pi, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, iFlow, Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, OpenCode, Qoder, Qwen, Trae, and more). Key capabilities:\n- Persistent multi-turn sessions scoped to git repos\n- Named parallel sessions (`-s backend`, `-s frontend`)\n- Queue-based prompt stacking with `--no-wait` fire-and-forget\n- `acpx flow run &lt;file&gt;` — TypeScript runtime for multi-step workflows with `acp` nodes, `action` steps, `decision` nodes\n- `--approve-all`, `--approve-reads`, `--deny-all` permission policies\n- `--format json` for structured output\n- Auto-resume with crash detection\n\n---\n\n## 3. MCP — Model Context Protocol\n\n**OpenClaw as MCP CLIENT (consuming servers):**\n- Native support added February 2026 using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.25.3`\n- Supports both stdio and HTTP/SSE transports\n- Compatible with the full 200+ community MCP server ecosystem\n- Config block in `openclaw.json`:\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"github\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"@modelcontextprotocol/server-github\"],\n      \"env\": {\"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN\": \"ghp_token\"}\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n- For HTTP/SSE: replace `command`/`args` with `url` and optional `headers`\n- MCP servers expose: **Resources** (data), **Tools** (actions), **Prompts** (templates)\n- Tools are auto-discovered and invoked by the agent without explicit code\n\n**OpenClaw as MCP SERVER (exposing to clients — `openclaw mcp serve`):**\n\nThis is a major underused capability. Running `openclaw mcp serve` starts a stdio MCP server that **exposes OpenClaw's full Gateway to external MCP clients** (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Zed, Cline, Windsurf).\n\nExposed tools:\n- `conversations_list` — discover all routed conversations\n- `conversation_get` — single conversation by session key\n- `messages_read` — full transcript history\n- `attachments_fetch` — non-text content metadata\n- `events_poll` / `events_wait` — live event streaming with cursor\n- `messages_send` — send through existing session routes\n- `permissions_list_open` / `permissions_respond` — manage exec/plugin approvals\n\nEvent types in-queue: `message`, `exec_approval_requested`, `exec_approval_resolved`, `plugin_approval_requested`, `plugin_approval_resolved`, `claude_permission_request`\n\nClaude-specific: when `--claude-channel-mode` is on, the server emits `notifications/claude/channel` (transcript messages as notifications) and `notifications/claude/channel/permission` (converts yes/no approval prompts).\n\n**This means Claude Code can connect to an OpenClaw Gateway as an MCP server and: send messages to WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord contacts, spawn sub-agents, manage cron jobs, control paired mobile devices (camera, GPS, commands), search memory, and respond to approval requests.**\n\nCommunity MCP server (`github.com/Helms-AI/openclaw-mcp-server`) exposes this via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` + `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. `openclaw serve` / Headless Server Mode\n\nThere is no distinct `openclaw serve` command in the open-source version. The equivalent is running the Gateway as a daemon:\n- Development: `openclaw gateway` (foreground)\n- Production: launchd (macOS) or systemd (Linux) supervision\n\nThe Gateway binds to `127.0.0.1:18789` by default. For remote access, use SSH tunnel or Tailscale. The **Web Control UI** is served directly from the Gateway at the same port (no separate web server).\n\n**`openclaw dashboard --no-open`** — headless start that prints the URL without opening a browser. Used in CI/container deployments.\n\n**Headless node role:** Any client can connect with `role: node` to the Gateway WebSocket, declaring capabilities. This is how iOS/Android/Raspberry Pi nodes work. Headless nodes can expose commands and receive `node.invoke` requests from the agent.\n\n**xAI device-code OAuth** (May 2026 release): supports \"remote and headless setups\" without browser callbacks — relevant for headless VPS deployments.\n\n**KiloClaw's \"serve\":** KiloClaw is Kilo's hosted OpenClaw — a dedicated VM (2 shared vCPUs, 3 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD) running the actual unforked OpenClaw in a managed environment with 5-layer tenant isolation, AES-256 encrypted credential vaults, tool allow-lists, and agent-mediated access (no direct SSH). The VM has shell access, persistent storage, headless browser, cron scheduling, and cross-session memory.\n\n---\n\n## 5. `kilo remote` / Remote Session Sharing\n\n`kilo remote` is not a distinct OpenClaw CLI command. \"Remote\" in OpenClaw refers to the Gateway connection mode for clients that aren't on the same machine.\n\n**Remote architecture modes:**\n1. **Direct mode** — Trusted LAN/Tailnet: `gateway.remote.transport: \"direct\"`, `url: \"ws://192.168.0.202:18789\"`\n2. **SSH tunnel** — `ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 user@host` then connect to localhost\n3. **Tailscale Serve** — Expose Gateway safely within tailnet with HTTPS\n4. **Cloud Relay** (feature request, issue #55915) — `openclaw login` OAuth + background heartbeat + WebSocket relay acceptance for mobile access without Tailscale\n\nThe macOS operator app uses direct LAN/Tailnet when reachable, SSH tunneling as fallback.\n\n**Real-time session sharing** is handled through the Gateway's WebSocket event subscription system — multiple clients connect and subscribe to the same session events. There is no dedicated \"session sharing\" UI, but the WebSocket protocol supports multiple concurrent operator clients.\n\n---\n\n## 6. `kilo acp` / ACP Server Mode\n\n`kilo acp` is not a separate command from `openclaw acp`. In the KiloClaw context, it refers to running OpenClaw's built-in ACP bridge against a KiloClaw-hosted Gateway.\n\n**What `openclaw acp` enables:**\n- Any ACP-speaking IDE (Zed natively; VS Code via extension; others via CLI) can drive an OpenClaw Gateway session\n- IDE sends prompts → ACP bridge → Gateway WebSocket → LLM → tool execution → streaming response back to IDE\n- The Gateway session persists between IDE restarts (reconnect with `--session-label`)\n- IDE's prompts route to whatever agent/model/toolset is configured in the Gateway\n\n**Key insight:** Because the Gateway owns multi-channel context (your WhatsApp messages, Telegram threads, email via Gmail PubSub, cron results), the IDE agent has access to all that context — **your coding agent in Zed can read your WhatsApp conversation history and trigger cross-channel actions**.\n\n**`OPENCLAW_SHELL=acp`** environment variable — enables shell profiles to apply ACP-specific context rules, restricting permissions for untrusted ACP operations.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Plugin System\n\n**Plugin types (six capability shapes):**\n1. **Channel plugins** — New messaging platforms\n2. **Provider plugins** — Alternative LLM endpoints (Ollama, OpenRouter, custom)\n3. **Tool plugins** — Custom capabilities; built with `defineToolPlugin`, scaffolded via `plugins init`\n4. **Hook packs** — Expose `openclaw.hooks` in `package.json`\n5. **Compatible bundles** — Support Codex, Claude Code, Cursor manifest formats\n6. **Skill bundles** — Skills, Claude command-skills, settings defaults, LSP server declarations\n\n**Manifest:** `openclaw.plugin.json` with inline JSON Schema (configSchema required even if empty). Machine-managed install metadata in `plugins/installs.json`.\n\n**Available conversation hooks:**\n- `llm_input` — Modify prompts before they hit the model\n- `llm_output` — Post-process model outputs\n- `before_model_resolve` — Override model selection\n- `before_agent_reply` — Intercept before response delivery\n- `before_agent_run` — Pre-execution setup\n- `before_agent_finalize` — Post-execution cleanup\n- `agent_end` — Session completion handler\n\nThese hooks require explicit `plugins.entries.&lt;id&gt;.hooks.allowConversationAccess=true`.\n\n**Installation sources:** `clawhub:&lt;package&gt;`, `npm:&lt;package&gt;`, `git:github.com/owner/repo@ref`, local paths, `.zip`/`.tgz`/`.tar.gz` archives.\n\n**May 2026 new commands:** `openclaw plugins build`, `openclaw plugins validate`, `openclaw plugins init` for typed tool plugin development.\n\n**ClawHub marketplace:** `clawhub.ai/plugins` — 50+ listed, 100 total, growing. Notable plugins:\n\n| Plugin | What it does |\n|--------|-------------|\n| Memory Graph (@klsgg) | Zero-config SQLite knowledge graph memory |\n| Spark Memory (@zellin) | Pattern detection from decision history |\n| Honcho Memory (@honcho-ai) | Persistent agent learning |\n| Lobster (@openclaw) | Typed pipelines + resumable approvals (built-in but also as plugin) |\n| Flow Weaver (@synergenius) | Deterministic compile-once workflows |\n| Stigmergy Scheduler (@stigmergy) | Pressure-field scheduling (replaces timer polling) |\n| TeamClaw (@teamclaws) | Virtual software team orchestration |\n| Agent Permissions (@clawnify) | Tool-call interception + approval flows |\n| AxonFlow Governance (@axonflow) | Policy enforcement + PII/secrets scanning |\n| OpenClaw Shield (@upx-us) | SIEM via Google Chronicle |\n| Clawthority (@clawthority) | Authorization policy engine |\n| TraceProof Runtime (@traceproof) | Message proof verification + audit trails |\n| Carbon-Aware Deferral (@vitalini) | Schedule tasks for cleanest grid hours |\n| Legal Data (@alexbloch-ia) | 66 official sources, 100+ countries |\n| Linear Agent Plugin | Webhook-driven AI pipeline with OAuth, multi-agent routing, issue triage |\n\nWhat plugins can do that built-in features cannot:\n- Intercept and rewrite every message before/after model invocation (`llm_input`/`llm_output`)\n- Override model selection at runtime (`before_model_resolve`)\n- Register new HTTP routes on the Gateway\n- Register new Gateway RPC methods\n- Run as persistent background services within the Gateway process\n- Expose new channel types (entire new platforms)\n- Add custom embedding/memory backends\n\n---\n\n## 8. Worktree System\n\nOpenClaw does not have a built-in git worktree subsystem. Worktrees are handled via:\n\n1. **The `git-worktree-manager` skill** (ClawHub: `lobehub.com/skills/openclaw-skills-git-worktree-manager`) — standardizes branch isolation, port allocation, environment sync, and cleanup so each worktree behaves like an independent local app.\n\n2. **Multi-agent routing with isolated workspaces** — Each agent instance in `openclaw.json` has its own `agentDir` (workspace), so you configure multiple agents pointing to different worktrees.\n\n3. **`sessions_spawn` with `cwd` override** — Sub-agents can be spawned with a specific working directory, effectively routing them to a worktree.\n\n4. **Multi-repo dispatch pattern** — When an issue is tagged with repo names, worker agents get isolated worktrees for each repo; one issue can work across multiple codebases in parallel.\n\n**Session isolation by design:** Each sub-agent session (`agent:&lt;agentId&gt;:subagent:&lt;uuid&gt;`) has its own context window, execution environment, conversation history, and tool access. Sub-agents cannot see the main chat. Results announce back to the requester via `sessions_send`.\n\n**Depth limit:** Sub-agents at depth ≥ 1 can spawn children (orchestrator mode). Depth 2 cannot spawn — `sessions_spawn` is denied at leaf level.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Session Import/Export\n\n**Storage format:** JSONL (one event per line), stored at `~/.openclaw/sessions/`. Append-only with branching support.\n\n**Export formats:** JSONL, CSV, JSON (full tree structure). Filter by agent, time range, users, or platform.\n\n**Session reset archiving:** Since February/March 2026, manual `/new`/`/reset` and daily resets archive old transcripts as `&lt;session&gt;.jsonl.reset.&lt;timestamp&gt;` — data is not lost, just renamed.\n\n**`sessions_history` tool:** Returns processed transcript (thinking tags removed, memory scaffolding stripped, tool-call XML eliminated, credentials masked, long blocks truncated). Returns flags: `truncated`, `droppedMessages`, `contentTruncated`, `contentRedacted`, `bytes`.\n\n**Import:** Community skill `github.com/dashhuang/openclaw-chat-history-import` imports external chat history (ChatGPT, Claude) into archive, daily memory, and MEMORY.md workflows. No native first-party import UI yet.\n\n**Session compaction:** Automatic — older conversations summarized via LLM with optional \"memory flush\" promoting durable information to MEMORY.md before condensation.\n\n**No universal \"export then reimport\" button yet** — this is a known gap (issue #45003).\n\n---\n\n## 10. The Lobster Workflow Engine\n\nThe most underused built-in power feature. Lobster is a typed, local-first DAG workflow engine embedded in-process within the Gateway.\n\n**Why it matters:** Agents avoid re-planning every step (token waste). Workflows are data (loggable, diffable, replayable). Side effects can be gated behind human approval checkpoints with durable resumption.\n\n**File format:** YAML (`.lobster` extension):\n```yaml\nname: inbox-triage\nargs:\n  tag:\n    default: \"family\"\nsteps:\n  - id: collect\n    command: inbox list --json\n  - id: categorize\n    command: inbox categorize --json\n    stdin: $collect.stdout\n  - id: approve\n    command: inbox apply --approve\n    stdin: $categorize.stdout\n    approval: required\n    condition: $approve.approved\n```\n\n**Step options:** `cwd`, `env`, `stdin`, `when`, `condition`, `retry`, `timeout_ms`, `on_error`\n\n**LLM integration:**\n```yaml\n- id: summarize\n  pipeline: llm.invoke --prompt 'Summarize this' --provider openclaw\n```\n\n**Agent triggers Lobster:**\n```json\n{\"action\": \"run\", \"pipeline\": \"/path/to/workflow.lobster\", \"argsJson\": \"{\\\"tag\\\":\\\"family\\\"}\"}\n```\n\n**Approval gate + resumption:**\n- Paused workflow returns `requiresApproval.resumeToken`\n- Resume: `{\"action\": \"resume\", \"token\": \"&lt;token&gt;\", \"approve\": true}`\n- Output envelope: `ok` | `needs_approval` | `cancelled`\n\n**Visualization:** `lobster graph --file workflow.lobster --format mermaid|dot|ascii`\n\n**Argument safety:** All args available as `LOBSTER_ARG_&lt;NAME&gt;` env vars; full args as `LOBSTER_ARGS_JSON`. Use env vars instead of raw `${arg}` substitution for safety.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Gateway WebSocket Protocol — Programmatic Control\n\nThis is the deepest capability. The Gateway is fully programmable via WebSocket protocol v4.\n\n**Handshake:**\n1. Gateway sends pre-connect challenge (nonce + timestamp)\n2. Client sends `connect` with role, scopes, device identity, auth\n3. Gateway returns `hello-ok` with protocol version, policy limits, session snapshot, device token\n\n**Frame types:**\n- Request: `{type:\"req\", id, method, params}`\n- Response: `{type:\"res\", id, ok, payload|error}`\n- Event: `{type:\"event\", event, payload, seq?, stateVersion?}`\n\n**Complete RPC method catalog:**\n\n| Category | Methods |\n|----------|---------|\n| System | `health`, `diagnostics.stability`, `status`, `gateway.identity.get`, `system-presence` |\n| Models | `models.list`, `usage.status`, `usage.cost`, `doctor.memory.*`, `sessions.usage*` |\n| Channels | `channels.status`, `channels.logout`, `web.login.start/wait`, `push.test` |\n| Voice/TTS | `talk.catalog`, `talk.config`, `talk.session.*`, `talk.mode`, `talk.speak`, `tts.*`, `voicewake.get/set` |\n| Config | `secrets.reload/resolve`, `config.get/set/patch/apply`, `config.schema*` |\n| Sessions | `sessions.list`, `sessions.subscribe`, `sessions.messages.*`, `sessions.describe`, `sessions.create`, `sessions.send`, `sessions.steer`, `sessions.abort`, `chat.history`, `chat.send`, `chat.abort` |\n| Nodes | `node.pair.*`, `node.list`, `node.describe`, `node.rename`, `node.invoke`, `node.invoke.result`, `node.event`, `node.pending.*` |\n| Approvals | `exec.approval.*`, `exec.approvals.*`, `plugin.approval.*` |\n| Agents/Skills | `agents.*`, `commands.list`, `skills.*`, `tools.catalog`, `tools.effective`, `tools.invoke` |\n| Automation | `wake`, `cron.*`, `tasks.*` |\n| Devices | `device.pair.*`, `device.token.rotate/revoke` |\n\n**Roles:**\n- `operator` — control plane (CLI, web UI, macOS app); scopes: `operator.read`, `operator.write`, `operator.admin`, `operator.approvals`, `operator.pairing`, `operator.talk.secrets`\n- `node` — capability host (iOS/Android/headless); declares `caps`, `commands`, `permissions`\n\n**Limits:** 30-second request timeout, 25 MB max payload, 52 MB max buffered bytes, 120 sessions/10-second rate limit, 2 MB payload validation.\n\n**Idempotency keys** required for all side-effecting operations (safe retries).\n\n---\n\n## 12. A2UI / Live Canvas\n\nAn agent-driven visual workspace — a dedicated server process (default port 18793) that provides isolation from the Gateway.\n\n**How it works:**\n- Agent generates HTML with A2UI attributes for interactive elements\n- Client renders HTML natively (macOS WebKit, iOS SwiftUI, Android WebView, web browsers)\n- User interactions in the canvas are forwarded back to the agent as tool calls\n- Agent can push UI updates in real time without user prompt\n\n**Use cases:** Progress trackers for long-running tasks, step-by-step approval wizards, live dashboards, data visualization, status monitors.\n\n**Gateway hosts:** Canvas at `/__openclaw__/canvas/` and A2UI at `/__openclaw__/a2ui/`.\n\n---\n\n## 13. Automation System: Cron vs. Heartbeat\n\n**Cron jobs:** Precise schedules for isolated runs. Definitions persist to disk (survive Gateway restarts). Each cron job can run in its own isolated session (own context window). May 2026: cron runs on a \"cron-owned wake lane\" to prevent blocking human chat.\n\n**HEARTBEAT.md:** The agent reads this file on each heartbeat tick and executes listed tasks. If nothing needs attention, replies `HEARTBEAT_OK` (silently dropped). Cost-efficient: batches multiple monitoring checks into one LLM turn. Runs in the main session context.\n\n**Rule:** Use Heartbeat for ambient monitoring (inbox check, calendar review, alert watching). Use Cron for precision-timed isolated jobs (daily reports, weekly summaries).\n\n---\n\n## 14. What KiloClaw Adds Over Bare OpenClaw\n\nKiloClaw is NOT a fork — it runs unmodified OpenClaw on managed infrastructure:\n\n| Feature | KiloClaw |\n|---------|---------|\n| Infrastructure | 2 vCPUs, 3 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD dedicated VM |\n| Model access | 500+ models via Kilo Gateway at zero markup |\n| Automation recipes | 610+ pre-built recipes |\n| Marketplace | ClawHub skill marketplace |\n| Security | 5-layer tenant isolation, AES-256 credential vaults, tool allow-lists |\n| Access | No direct SSH — agent-mediated only |\n| Provisioning | Under 5 minutes, no CLI required |\n| Credentials | Automated API key generation + refresh via KiloCode |\n\n---\n\n## 15. Non-Obvious and Underused Capabilities\n\n**Claude Code → OpenClaw MCP bridge** (the biggest missed opportunity): By running `openclaw mcp serve` and registering it as an MCP server in Claude Code, Claude Code gains: WhatsApp/Telegram send, sub-agent spawning, cron management, paired device control (camera/GPS/commands), Gateway health, memory search, TTS. This makes Claude Code a front-end for the entire OpenClaw sovereign stack.\n\n**`sessions_send` with `maxPingPongTurns`:** Enables up to 20-turn reply loops between agents — structured multi-agent dialogue without manual orchestration.\n\n**`sessions_yield`:** Agent ends its turn and waits for the sub-agent's completion result as the next message — no polling, no busy-wait.\n\n**`sessions_spawn` with `context: \"fork\"`:** Child agent inherits the requester's full transcript as context. Useful for \"continuation\" agents.\n\n**`sessions_spawn` with `runtime: \"acp\"`:** Spawns an external harness (Claude Code, Codex) as the sub-agent instead of the built-in LLM runtime. This makes OpenClaw the orchestrator for external coding agents.\n\n**Codex plugin management in OpenClaw (May 2026):** `/codex plugins list/enable/disable` — OpenClaw can manage Codex's own plugin ecosystem from within the chat interface.\n\n**`openclaw mcp list|show|set|unset`:** Manage MCP server definitions in config without editing JSON manually.\n\n**Provider failover:** Runtime model swapping between providers (GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet/Opus, Gemma 4 local). Cost-optimize per workflow step.\n\n**Append-only session logs with branching:** Sessions support conversation recovery and inspection. The branching model means you can fork a conversation at any point.\n\n**Skill precedence:** Workspace skills (`./skills/`) override globally installed ones. This means per-project skill customization without touching global config.\n\n**`openclaw audit --skill`:** Audit any skill before installation to inspect its capability declarations.\n\n**`openclaw qa coverage --tools`:** Tool-fixture coverage reporting for testing agent harnesses.\n\n**Discord Voice follow (May 2026):** Agent follows configured users into voice channels with multi-user handoff.\n\n**Apple Watch approval workflow (v2026319):** ~8-second wrist-based approval for critical agent actions.\n\n**Prediction market betting (v2026410):** Agents wager on Polymarket/Augur with configurable daily budget limits.\n\n---\n\n## 16. Community-Discovered Creative Combinations\n\n1. **Multi-agent software pipeline:** Three agents (programmer/reviewer/tester) orchestrated via Lobster workflows — programmer spawns via `sessions_spawn`, reviewer gets `context: \"fork\"`, tester runs in sandbox. No human intervention after initial task assignment.\n\n2. **Idea-to-decision overnight cron:** Cron fires at 2am, spawns sub-agents per idea captured throughout the day (from Telegram messages), each sub-agent researches alternatives, results `sessions_send` back to orchestrator, morning briefing delivered to WhatsApp.\n\n3. **STATE.yaml multi-agent pattern:** Shared YAML file acts as coordination surface between parallel agents. Each agent reads/writes its section. No direct agent-to-agent messaging needed — file becomes the shared state.\n\n4. **n8n credential isolation:** Agent delegates API calls to n8n workflows via webhooks — agent never holds API credentials directly. n8n handles OAuth, agent just invokes webhook endpoints.\n\n5. **Self-healing home server:** Agent has SSH node paired to home server. Cron checks server health. On failure, agent SSHes in, diagnoses, remediates. Alerting via Telegram. Full autonomous recovery loop.\n\n6. **Raspberry Pi IoT integration:** OpenClaw on Pi connected to WHOOP health wearable + Home Assistant via Ollama (local models, no API costs). No cloud dependency for home automation.\n\n7. **Claude Code as OpenClaw IDE:** Register `openclaw mcp serve` as MCP server in Claude Code → Claude Code gains full Gateway control. Claude Code becomes the terminal UI for an OpenClaw sovereign stack.\n\n8. **acpx flow orchestration:** Use `acpx flow run` YAML files to define multi-step workflows combining `acp` nodes (Claude Code doing the coding work), `action` steps (git operations, test runners), `decision` nodes (pass/fail branching) — deterministic CI-like pipelines driven by AI.\n\n9. **Lobster approval-gated deployment pipeline:** Code review → test run → approval gate (human reviews summary) → deploy. Lobster manages the DAG, surfaces the approval request to the agent, agent delivers it to Telegram for human approval, resume token triggers deploy.\n\n10. **Multi-channel unified inbox:** WhatsApp Business + Instagram + Email + Google Reviews all routed to same OpenClaw agent. Agent responds 24/7 across all channels from single configuration. Customer never knows which channel is AI vs. human.\n\n---\n\n## Implications for PCC (Phoenix-Command-Consul)\n\nThe most powerful architecture for PCC based on this research:\n\n1. **OpenClaw as the sovereign command bus:** Gateway on a persistent host, connected to Telegram (primary control channel), Discord (team operations), and potentially WhatsApp.\n\n2. **Claude Code → OpenClaw via MCP:** Register `openclaw mcp serve` as an MCP server in Claude Code settings. Claude Code (your current interface) gains direct Gateway control: can spawn sub-agents, send messages to any channel, manage cron jobs, query memory.\n\n3. **acpx as the inter-agent protocol layer:** Use `acpx` to dispatch tasks to different coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, KiloCode) from OpenClaw orchestration, with named sessions scoped per project/task.\n\n4. **Lobster for deterministic pipelines:** Any repeatable multi-step workflow (pipeline run, harvest-extract, soul ingestion, ledger sync) should be a `.lobster` file. Approval gates for D1 writes and canonical commits.\n\n5. **sessions_spawn for parallel workstreams:** Parallel CANON processing (RRL, Soul, DNA, HL) as simultaneous sub-agents, each isolated, results yielded back to orchestrator.\n\n6. **HEARTBEAT.md for ambient monitoring:** D1 health check, SOULCOUNT delta monitoring, pipeline queue depth — all in heartbeat, batched into one LLM turn every 30 minutes.\n\nThe key insight: **OpenClaw is not a coding assistant. It is a sovereign agent runtime that can orchestrate coding assistants.** PCC should treat OpenClaw as the command layer and Claude Code / KiloCode as execution workers dispatched via ACP.\n\n---\n\nSources:\n- [GitHub -
